summary: A game-agnostic toolkit for Sega Saturn ports to PC: disc reader, SH-2 decoder and interpreter, function discovery for SHC, GCC and SGL code, a static recompiler to C++, and a runtime that replaces both SH-2s, VDP1 and VDP2 in software, the SCU, SMPC, CD block, 68000 and SCSP. Proven on six games; its furthest ports are played into their first area with sound.
highlights: 6 ports built on it
Virtual Hydlide: 10,259 functions, 1.5 million instructions recompiled; 51,532 test vectors, 0 diffs
SH-2 decoder checked on all 65,536 16-bit words against capstone
measure: 100 % = every subsystem stood in for, proven by a finished port
progress_basis: In: both SH-2s, VDP1/VDP2 in software (NBG0-3, RBG0, line scroll, raster effects), SCU, SMPC, CD block with seek timing, 68000 and SCSP. Missing per README: VDP1 on the GPU, RBG1, sprite window, vertical cell scroll, mosaic, MIDI, SH-2 on-chip interrupts and caches. Best ports (Virtual Hydlide, DoDonPachi) are played in their first area/stage, no further.

title: Rudra no Hihou (Treasure of the Rudras)
tagline: A devlog of decoding the Japanese text system of Rudra no Hihou, and a static rip of its AKAO music
summary: A reverse-engineering devlog on the Japanese text system of Rudra no Hihou / Treasure of the Rudras: single-byte kana, two-byte kanji, a DTE substring dictionary, a name dictionary and inline furigana. A second track documents the AKAO-family sound engine and a fully static extractor that rebuilds every song's APU image from the ROM tables alone. No ROM data included.
highlights: About 286 of the game's about 730 kanji codes identified
Two-byte kanji on lead bytes $01-$03, roughly ordered by frequency ($0101 = 言)
Every song's APU image rebuilt from the ROM tables alone, with no emulator
progress_basis: Text structure is decoded but only about 286 of about 730 kanji codes are identified (39 %); the sound-engine track reached a fully static extractor. README calls it ongoing and hobby-paced.

title: Tales of Phantasia (SNES / GBA)
tagline: 48 Mbit ExHiROM cart and the 2003 GBA rebuild: no file system, LZSS codec specified
summary: Documents both Japanese cartridges. The SNES cart has no enhancement chip and no file system; the GBA version is a rebuild that inherited a 1 KiB metatile table byte for byte.
highlights: 1,089 codec blocks found; 74/74 verified decodes
SPC700 boot payload: 14,551 of 14,551 bytes accounted for
Only 20 of 817 ExHiROM-extension blocks indexed
progress_basis: Many items are Verified, but the README lists the Japanese script and font as not located and 797 of 817 extension blocks as unaccounted.
first: README says it is one of only two commercial ExHiROM games.

title: Tales block codec
tagline: The nine-byte-header LZSS used across Tales titles 1995-2011, with a reference decoder
summary: Specification and reference decoder (tales_block.py) for Wolf Team's in-house LZSS, plus the per-build lineage evidence from 1995 to 2021. A verification table covers decoders and constant scans across all documented builds.
highlights: 1,089 blocks decode on the 1995 SFC image; 101,397 across ten disc images
47,513 of 47,513 blocks on Tales of the Abyss
0 blocks in 9.04 GB of Tales of Xillia
progress_basis: The Verification section lists mostly exact-match results (all blocks decode, byte-for-byte cross-checks); remaining open items concern origin and why builds differ. No explicit tally is given, so the value is a judgment.
first: README says the codebase, not the machine or the date, is the boundary, and that engine and codec are separable.

title: Tales series index
tagline: Index of 19 Tales titles across ten platforms, organised by saga around the shared block codec
summary: Series index for the Tales documentation repos, in release order from 1995 to 2021, with a verbatim write-up per title. Organised by saga because the shared LZSS codec spans more platforms than any platform has Tales titles.
highlights: 19 titles listed, one repository each
Ten platforms, 1995 to 2021
One shared codec document linked from every title
progress_basis: All 19 listed titles have a linked documentation repo; no planned-but-missing titles are stated. Depth varies (Berseria row is one line).

title: tg16kit
tagline: PC Engine static recompilation: a HuC6280-to-C++ recompiler and VDC/VCE/PSG runtime that run all 423 HuCards
summary: Reverse engineering and static recompilation for the PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16: HuCards and mappers, a HuC6280 disassembler, a tracer, a HuC6280-to-C++ recompiler built for the MMU, raster interrupts and block transfers, and a runtime with the VDC, VCE, SuperGrafx VPC and PSG. All 423 cards in MAME's lists run frame for frame identical to the interpreter.
highlights: All 423 HuCards (325 PC Engine, 93 TurboGrafx-16, 5 SuperGrafx) run identical over 6,000 frames
140 never touch the interpreter; 402 interpret fewer than 100 instructions a frame
No ports table: a library-wide kit; PSG sound with six channels, DDA and noise
measure: 100 % = every cartridge of the set runs identically
progress_basis: README: all 423 cards MAME's software lists know run frame-identical in lockstep (423/423). Not covered: the CD-ROM² library (not in the HuCard set), multitap and other controllers, backup RAM, mid-line video effects; sound a first pass.

title: Undertow
tagline: High-level emulator for the ZAPiT Game Wave: the discs' Lua 5.0.2 bytecode on a reimplemented ZIT engine
summary: An emulator for the ZAPiT Game Wave, the Canadian DVD-based console. Game Wave games are Lua 5.0.2 bytecode run by the ZIT engine on each disc; Undertow runs that bytecode on a lightly patched Lua and reimplements the engine's libraries on SDL2 and FFmpeg, so no firmware is needed. It ships zbcc, a homebrew compiler, and hosts a Doom written as a Game Wave script.
highlights: 10 titles playable: 9 of the 16-disc Redump set plus the late Indian release Quiz Konnect
MPEG-2 movies with sound, OSD overlays, disc fonts, 32 KB save EEPROM, up to 6 remotes
No firmware or BIOS needed: the engine's gl, text, movie, audio and input libraries are reimplemented
measure: 100 % = the known library playable, with sound
progress_basis: Status table lists 10 playable titles, 9 of them from the 16-disc Redump set (Letter Zap!'s Tag! untested); the other Redump titles are untested, and parabola/blinking animations and deinterlacing are not done.

title: VIS File Viewer
tagline: Media viewer for the Tandy VIS: a disc's photos, WAV and MIDI audio, and FLC video on an 80286
summary: A single Win16 NE executable that can be the shell of any VIS disc: it lists the media on the CD and plays it with the console's native Modular Windows facilities. Retail VIS discs carry no AVI, so it includes a from-scratch Autodesk FLC/FLI player that decodes straight into video RAM, paced off the PIT.
highlights: Photos via StretchDIBits, WAV and MIDI via MCI, FLC/FLI video via DISPDIB DVA writes to A000
Inspection of three retail VIS discs found no AVI file at all, only FLC and RLE/DIB video
GDI full-frame video ran at ~1-5 fps; direct A000 decoding and PIT pacing lift that ceiling
progress_basis: Evidence is thin: the README has no status section; it describes the three media types as working under MAME with build tools for adding media. No release or real-hardware run is mentioned.

title: Tandy VIS disc documentation index
tagline: Index of the Tandy/Memorex VIS disc write-ups: four pressings documented, two more in hand.
summary: Index of the VIS disc documentation, one repository per pressing, feeding the shared platform checklist. It also holds the four-test G1-G4 criterion for whether a disc is a game, applied to each entry. No disc images or assets are included.
highlights: 4 pressings documented, 2 more retail pressings in hand with CONTROL.TAT compared
G1-G4 game test: Race the Clock 4 of 4, Hosea Freeman 3 of 4, Links 4 of 4 (amended)
progress_basis: README states four titles documented and two more pressings in hand (4 of 6); other VIS titles are mentioned as existing but not counted.

title: Links: The Challenge of Golf
tagline: The VIS pressing of Links, whose MDmd archive container is opened and 320 of 320 members decoded.
summary: Documentation of the 3.9 MB VIS pressing of Links. It derives the MDmd recursive archive and its variable-width LZW codec, shows GIFM is a GIF over raw indices, and finds 197 of 197 shared members byte-identical to the MS-DOS release. No product bytes are published.
highlights: 320 of 320 members decode to their declared length, residue 0 on 9 of 9 archives
197 of 197 shared archive members identical to the MS-DOS release
Sector 1667 has non-zero reserved field and failing P and Q parity, unexplained
progress_basis: All 13 files and 9 archives are opened with residue 0; one sector and the TITLE.SCR colouring remain unexplained, and open score is 19.25 of 24.50.

title: Tandy / Memorex VIS platform checklist
tagline: Platform checklist for the Tandy VIS using three marks: measured on discs, proven by authoring, or unverified.
summary: The canonical VIS checklist, shared by every VIS write-up. It separates findings measured on retail pressings from findings proven by writing code for the console, and keeps contradictions visible instead of resolving them.
highlights: Three marks: [N of 5], [authoring], [unverified]
CONTROL.TAT: 84 bytes byte-identical across three unrelated discs
3 of 5 discs in hand are documented
progress_basis: README: 3 documented discs of 5 in hand; six [authoring] items remain, and most disc marks are [1 of 4] to [4 of 4] with small samples.

title: Race the Clock
tagline: A bilingual vocabulary game on VIS: 1,208 AVI files, of which 80.29 % of the disc is copies.
summary: Documentation of Race the Clock, a Win16 NE application on VIS with 3,625 files. It shows 1,208 genuine Video for Windows files, reassembles 40 boards from 2,405 DIBs, and finds a retail title importing HC.DLL. No product bytes are published.
highlights: 1,314 distinct SHA-1 = 19.7139 % of content; 80.2861 % is duplication
1,208 AVI, BI_RLE8, two streams each, 13 m 12.53 s of distinct footage
Open score 53.5 of 71; leftovers: four solved, three unexplained
progress_basis: README gives full content accounting by denominator, but chapter 15 leaves three leftovers unexplained and the open scorecard is 53.5 of 71.
first: Second documented VIS pressing; first with AVI files and an HC.DLL import in a retail title

title: Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, Vol. I
tagline: The first retail VIS disc opened here: 96.43 % is .IMV video in a format derived from scratch.
summary: Byte-level documentation of the VIS pressing of Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, Vol. I. The .IMV block-chain format is derived and verified on 157 of 157 files, and the disc contains a DOS executable and no Windows one. No product bytes are published.
highlights: 96.4344 % of 445,760,838 bytes is .IMV: 1 h 48 m 35 s at 15 fps
size[i-1] == prev[i] holds on 157 of 157 .IMV files, 3,879 segments
Image: 218,004 of 218,004 sectors clean on EDC, ECC P and Q
progress_basis: Format derived and checked, but the picture source is stated as unsettled and chapter 17 records stopping at 99.84 % of the picture; 300 written sectors are unclaimed.
first: First retail VIS disc opened in this collection

title: VIS Synth
tagline: OPL3 polyphonic synth for the Tandy VIS: pad instrument, MIDI file player and live MIDI through a MAME bridge
summary: An OPL3 synthesizer for the Tandy/Memorex VIS (Modular Windows 3.1 on an 80286), as Win16 NE programs driving the YMF262 directly through ports 0x388/0x389. Three versions: an 8-voice instrument on the hand controller, a format-0 MIDI file player, and live MIDI from a host keyboard through a custom MAME ISA card.
highlights: v0: 8-voice OPL3 polyphony on the 8-button hand controller
v2: SMF format-0 parser, voice allocator and PIT-timed scheduler, playing from CD-ROM
v3: custom ROM-free, MPU-401-UART-compatible MAME ISA bridge for live MIDI (emulator only)
progress_basis: All three milestones are marked working in the status table; v0 and v2 run on stock MAME and are marked portable to a real VIS, v3 is emulator-only. No release or real-hardware run is mentioned.

title: The Secrets of Hosea Freeman
tagline: A VIS treasure-hunt CD through a New Bedford whaling house, documented down to residue 0.
summary: Documentation of a 1992 VIS pressing: 31 numbered rooms, 524 speech files and 59 RIFF/ANIM films. It derives the RIFF/ANIM format and finds the first DLL on any VIS pressing, which is the movie player. No product bytes are published.
highlights: 115,627 of 115,627 sectors pass all six mode1.py checks
236,804,096 bytes attributed, residue 0
Open-question scorecard: inherited 19.50 of 20, open 32.50 of 50
progress_basis: Accounting line says 236,804,096 bytes attributed with residue 0 and all formats derived; chapter 17 lists work not done and the open score is 32.50 of 50.
first: First .DLL on any VIS pressing; third documented VIS disc

title: Wolfenstein 3D
tagline: Wolfenstein 3D as a Win16 program on the Tandy/Memorex VIS, a 286 running Modular Windows
summary: A Wolfenstein 3D port to the 1992 Tandy/Memorex Video Information System, a 12 MHz 80286 running Modular Windows 3.1. It is written as a native Win16 program with its own raycaster following the vanilla source, OPL3 music and AdLib effects by direct port I/O, and digitised voices through the VIS DAC over raw DMA. Tested in MAME.
highlights: A direct A000 framebuffer via DispDib took it from 7-8 fps to 14-18 fps
Hand-controller key codes VK_HC1_* (0x70..0x79) found by experiment
Three-channel audio: IMF music, AdLib effects and Wolf3D voice samples on DMA channel 7
progress_basis: Milestones through A.26 are done: raycaster, doors, enemy AI, combat, pickups, HUD, music, effects and voices, judged 'playable' by the tester; only E1L1 is named and level progression and real hardware are not mentioned.

title: watarakit
tagline: Watara Supervision static recompilation: a W65C02-to-C++ recompiler that runs all 63 cartridges of the set
summary: Reverse engineering and static recompilation for the Watara Supervision: a cartridge reader, a W65C02 disassembler, a tracer that measures what a recompiler faces in each game, a W65C02-to-C++ recompiler and a runtime with sound. All 63 cartridges of the (USA, Europe) set run frame for frame identical to the interpreter.
highlights: All 63 cartridges recompiled and run identical to the interpreter over 6,000 frames each
45 of 63 never touch the interpreter
No ports table: a library-wide kit; sound covers two pulse channels, noise and sample DMA
measure: 100 % = every cartridge of the set runs identically
progress_basis: README: all 63 cartridges of the (USA, Europe) set recompiled, built and run frame-identical to the interpreter in lockstep for 6,000 frames each (63/63); no missing features listed.

title: Tales of Graces (Wii)
tagline: Wii disc STGJAF: the block codec returns, FPS4 archives, CPK bulk and an embedded DS ROM
summary: Documentation of the December 2009 Wii disc: 4,832 FPS4 archives, three CPK containers with zeroed CRILAYLA magic, and a complete Nintendo DS ROM shipped in /ds. The codec is present in two routines in main.dol.
highlights: 1,318 codec blocks decode, 1,162 to an FPS4 archive
7,115 of 7,115 CRILAYLA members reproduce their declared length
Project tag TO10 in nineteen spellings in main.dol
progress_basis: Most of the 20-odd claims are Verified; TSS, SE3 and MBIN formats and the .txm index layout are listed Open (counted, not decoded).
first: README says the disc names its developer, which no earlier build in the corpus did.

title: Tales of Symphonia: Dawn of the New World (Wii)
tagline: Wii disc RT4JAF: 13,386 files and a Tales build with no block codec
summary: Documents the Japanese Wii disc (4.29 GB game partition, 13,386 files, 1,506 MSCF archives). Its main result is that the block codec is absent, tested against the 2003 GameCube prequel with a byte-equality control.
highlights: 13,386 files, 17 h 42 m audio, 20 m 23 s video (70.10 % media)
Signature 5b 80 80 8d in 1,506 of 1,506 MSCF payloads
872-byte decoder search: 10 bytes here vs 835 bytes of shared SDK code
progress_basis: Disc layout and budget are Verified; the README lists the MSCF payload format, the reason for the codec's absence and the developing team as Open.
first: README says this build excluded the last surviving alternative explanation for the Nintendo DS zeros.

title: The Last Story
tagline: Format notes and tools for the LastWorld engine of The Last Story, checked against the running game
summary: Reverse-engineering notes and Python tools for the LastWorld engine of The Last Story. The pack format and its CRC path hash, text, textures, models, skinning, animation, maps, collision, effects and the full sound archive are documented with extractors; a Gekko SLEIGH for Ghidra lifts code coverage of main.dol from 44 % to 97.6 %. Results are checked against a running game.
highlights: 98.95 % of 7,717 voiced lines linked to their clip; the other 81 shown to be cut content
Gekko SLEIGH: Ghidra reads 97.6 % of main.dol instead of 44 %, 15,955 functions
A FIFO log decodes 555,010 of 555,010 bytes; 5,336 of 5,336 draws matched to their model
progress_basis: The stated goal (container, text, texture and audio formats with tools) is met and far exceeded; the README's 'not solved' list still holds several minor items (some effect channels, .gmk trigger types, .hcb type field, an equipment atlas).
first: As far as the author could verify, no public reverse-engineering material existed for this title before.

title: wiikit
tagline: Wii and GameCube toolkit: disc tools, a Gekko-to-C++ static recompiler and a runtime replacing the hardware
summary: A game-agnostic toolkit for Wii (and GameCube) ports to PC: disc, RVZ, DOL/ELF and RSO tools, a Gekko decoder, a static recompiler to C++ and a C++20/SDL3/OpenGL runtime standing in for the CPU, GX, DSP/AX, IOS, NAND and controllers. Every change is checked on every port; its first port, Victorious, has been played through to the credits.
highlights: 10 ports built on it (9 Wii games, 1 GameCube game)
Victorious: all 20,653 functions compile and link; the game played through to its credits
cw demangler: 20,619 of 20,619 function names; ppc: 1,658,815 instructions, none undecoded
measure: 100 % = every subsystem stood in for, proven by a finished port
progress_basis: In: disc/RVZ, DOL/ELF/RSO, recompiler with function discovery, CPU, GX/TEV/fog, EFB copies, DSP/AX audio, IOS/NAND, Remote, Nunchuk, Classic, GameCube DVD/ARAM/SI. Missing per README: EXI memory cards, early AX micro-code, locked-cache DMA, Remote motion, Z textures, /dev/net/wd. Best port: pc-victorious, played through (four episodes, finale, credits).

title: Crema
tagline: Clean-room GX2/AX engine for Wii U homebrew, with 14 examples verified on real hardware
summary: A clean-room engine for Wii U homebrew over GX2 and AX: runtime GLSL, cache-safe buffers and textures, fenced frame pacing, a sampler-based audio stack with ADPCM, saves, a scene stack and a .cpak archive. Every module was extracted from an example that needed it; four games in four genres stand on it, and the newest added no line to it.
highlights: Measured on console: 191.8 Mtris/s sustained and 3.76 Gpix/s fill, 85% of the R7xx ceiling
14 examples, from a triangle to a flight game and a 120 Hz football simulation, at 59.9-60 fps
Save to SD in 42-47 ms; a .cpak archive loads 356 KB in 32.33 ms against 38.95 ms loose
progress_basis: The README states every criterion it named for an engine is met (saving, scenes, a new genre needing no change) and all 14 examples are verified on real hardware; by its own rule it keeps growing only when a game asks, and has no editor by design.
first: To our knowledge, the first published GX2 polygon/fill throughput numbers measured from homebrew on real hardware.

title: Little Big Adventure 2
tagline: Twinsen's Odyssey on the Wii U from the 1997 Adeline source, completed start to finish on real hardware
summary: A native devkitPro/WUT port of the original 1997 source of Little Big Adventure 2 / Twinsen's Odyssey, with a platform backend and the little-endian data fixes a big-endian PowerPC needs. The game has been completed start to finish on a real Wii U, with every cutscene and FMV, at 50-80 fps, with GamePad touch controls. Bring your own assets.
highlights: V1.0: full playthrough on real Wii U hardware, intro to ending credits
50-80 fps on the console at a 960x720 blit
All Smacker FMVs stream from disk; the 76 MB intro never touches RAM
progress_basis: README-WIIU.md: V1.0, completed start to finish on real hardware, parity about 99.9 %; remaining items are polish only (control mapping, touch layout, a music-change hitch).

title: Planet Blupi
tagline: Planet Blupi on the Wii U under Aroma, with the GamePad touchscreen as the mouse
summary: A homebrew Wii U port of Planet Blupi, the 1997 Epsitec point-and-click strategy game, from Mathieu Schroeter's open-source SDL2 version. It is verified on real hardware and behaves identically to the PC original, with both campaigns, FMV transcoded to Cinepak and Ogg, and the attract-mode demos. The freeware assets are embedded, so no data has to be supplied.
highlights: Verified on real Wii U hardware, identical behaviour to the PC original
Self-contained .wuhb of about 130 MB with all freeware assets in the romfs
Every Wii U change behind #ifdef __WIIU__ or in a separate wiiu/ tree
progress_basis: README: playable and verified on real Wii U hardware, full mission and training campaigns, behaves identically to the PC original; only a right-click mapping is planned.

title: wskit
tagline: WonderSwan static recompilation: a V30MZ-to-C++ recompiler and runtime; 204 of 205 cartridges run identical
summary: Reverse engineering and static recompilation for the WonderSwan and WonderSwan Color: cartridge footer and banks, a V30MZ decoder cut down from fmtownskit's, a tracer, a V30MZ-to-C++ recompiler for segmented code and a runtime with display, sound, DMA, saves and RTC. 204 of 205 cartridges run 6,000 frames identical to the interpreter; the 205th crashes the same way in both.
highlights: 204 of 205 cartridges (110 WonderSwan, 95 Color) identical over 6,000 frames
202 never touch the interpreter
No ports table: a library-wide kit; MAME's V30MZ followed, prefetch queue included
measure: 100 % = every cartridge of the set runs identically
progress_basis: README: 204 of 205 cartridges run frame-identical for 6,000 frames; Youfu Makai matches up to frame 1581, where the game crashes under the monkey pad in both. Not covered: serial port, WonderWitch flash, Pocket Challenge V2; sound unchecked by ear.

title: Tales of Vesperia (Xbox 360)
tagline: Structural notes on the Japanese Xbox 360 disc: FPS4, XCompress and the 8,255-block Tales codec
summary: Documentation of the 7.84 GB XGD2 disc (title ID 0x4E4D07E9): 162 files holding 11,063 members, FPS4 containers, XCompress and the block codec. It is the fourteenth build in the codec corpus.
highlights: 8,255 of 8,255 codec blocks decode, 337,852,435 B to 775,930,739 B
6,128 XCompress streams, 3.33 GB to 11.67 GB
6 h 22 m of audio, 30 m 59 s of video, 30.84 % media
progress_basis: Byte budget tiles the image exactly and most claims are marked Verified; four claims remain Open (TL namespace date, codec retention, 334 MB on the older compressor, zero-length voice archives).
